sources.citation: Eberhard, Simons & Fennig (eds.). 2019 / 2021. Ethnologue, 22nd and 24th ed., entry 'Dugwor' (archived copies)
sources.note: Nothing; body paywalled, only names and classification (Afro-Asiatic > Chadic > Biu-Mandara > A > A.5) visible.

sources.citation: Friesen, Dianne. 2017. A grammar of Moloko. Berlin: Language Science Press (already held by the project)
sources.note: Mentions Dugwor only as a neighbouring language and in the classification tree; nothing about Dugwor stress.

sources.citation: SIL Language & Culture Archives, search listing for language code dme (capture 2015-09-18) and OLAC combined catalog for dme (capture 2020-07-16)
sources.note: Catalog listings only: the sole holdings for Dugwor are the two Brye survey reports (+ Glottolog and Ethnologue records). No phonology, grammar, dictionary or orthography guide is listed.

sources.citation: Brye, Edward & Elizabeth Brye. 2004. Rapid appraisal sociolinguistic research of Dugwor. SIL Electronic Survey Reports 2004-009. 18 pp.
sources.note: Published version of the 2001 survey already read; only worth downloading to confirm it adds nothing on phonology (PDF is open but could not be reached by automated download).

sources.citation: Brye, Edward & Elizabeth Brye. 2001. Rapid appraisal sociolinguistic research of Dugwor: ALCAM [162] (Diamaré Division, Far North Province). Yaoundé: SIL / Ministry of Scientific and Technical Research. 16 pp. (SIL Language & Culture Archives entry 47246)
sources.note: Nothing. Sociolinguistic survey (Feb 2000) with two 120-item Dougour/Mikiri wordlists in Appendix 1 (forms carry acute accents, unexplained, e.g. 'méy' mouth, 'ré' eye); the only phonology remark is 'There is no phonology. Any writing of the language is being done by those who attended school and are applying what they learned there.' (p. 8, §3.5.2, the scanned text). No word on stress, tone or accent.

sources.citation: Ousmanou. 2005. Esquisse phonologique du dugwor. Mémoire de Maîtrise/DEA, Département de Linguistique et Langues Africaines, Université de Yaoundé I.
sources.tag: likely states stress; not yet obtained
sources.access_detail: a digital copy exists, not open: the recorded link leads to a login, a search-only view or a restricted repository; the linked copy is not accessible
sources.note: The only phonological description of Dugwor known to Glottolog (listed by Glottolog as a phonology); a French 'esquisse phonologique' from Yaoundé I normally has a section on tons/accent and would carry the stress/tone statement if one exists.

sources.citation: Ousmanou. 1999. Phonologie du Dugwor. Yaoundé: SIL (ms.).
sources.tag: likely states stress; not yet obtained
sources.note: Named by Glottolog as possibly the same work as the 2005 thesis; an SIL Cameroon internal phonology write-up that would precede any orthography work. Not in the SIL archive listing for dme (2015) or OLAC (2020); would need a request to SIL Cameroon (Yaoundé) or the SIL Language & Culture Archives.

sources.citation: Barreteau, Daniel. 1987. Un essai de classification lexico-statistique des langues de la famille tchadique parlées au Cameroun. In Barreteau & Tourneux (eds.), Langues et cultures dans le bassin du lac Tchad, 43-77. Paris: ORSTOM.
sources.tag: likely states stress; not yet obtained
sources.note: Glottolog's subclassification source (p. 68); comparative wordlist work on the Mofu/Mafa group that may note whether the Dugwor data were tone-marked, but will not give a stress rule.
